operations.details_summary: Contains current-user automatic detection, PAC URL, proxy, and bypass settings.
The structure reflects user configuration only and may contain null or dynamically allocated strings; it is not proof of runtime use.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WINHTTP_PROXY_RESULT primary official Microsoft source verified.
Contains an ordered set of extended proxy resolution entries.
The returned list is a resolution result, not proof that a connection succeeded through any entry or that failover order was followed.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WINHTTP_PROXY_RESULT_ENTRY primary official Microsoft source verified.
Describes one proxy result entry including proxy, bypass, scheme, and port information.
A single entry is only one candidate route and does not authenticate the proxy or establish that it carried the observed response.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WinHttpCrackUrl primary official Microsoft source verified.
Separates a URL into scheme, host, port, path, and extra-info components.
URL parsing does not perform canonical DNS, IDN, proxy, redirect, or endpoint validation and must not be treated as connection identity.

URL_COMPONENTS primary official Microsoft source verified.
Defines component pointers and lengths used to parse or construct URLs.
Component buffers and lengths require strict initialization and bounds handling; equivalent textual URLs can still resolve or route differently.

Constructed URL text does not prove canonicalization, DNS resolution, transport security, redirect destination, or server identity.

Reports authentication schemes advertised by a server or proxy after an authentication challenge.
Advertised schemes are peer-controlled and do not prove credentials were accepted, confidentiality was established, or the peer is trusted.

Creates a proxy-resolver handle from an asynchronous WinHTTP session for extended proxy resolution.
A resolver handle is lifecycle state only and does not prove proxy discovery completed, a route was selected, or a request used that route.
